findings.where: the last take, frames 667-690, and the clip's own record at evidence/logs/08_state_propagating.json
findings.what: The one message that crosses a real disconnect arrives twice: the log's `said_again` reads [{"line": "message the bus is late, dont wait up", "times": 2}], and the matching `arrivals` entry records the thread going from 8078 rows to 8082 rows (+4) for the two lines `far` wrote while the link was cut (`state mood quiet` and `message the bus is late, dont wait up`, both at_frame 667); all 16 other arrivals in 06/07/08/15 add exactly +1 row and `said_again` is null in all three other clips.
findings.why: Row 01 says in terms: no dropped or duplicated messages, and correct ordering after going offline and reconnecting. This is a duplicate on the only reconnect anywhere in the set, recorded by the capture itself, so it is not an inference. reliability.json reports `duplicates: 0` and `offline_queue: 26 events queued offline, all delivered on reconnect`, but that is a headless harness on the local transport; the one time the same fault is exercised on the glass, the message lands twice. A partner who has to scroll back and work out which of two identical notes was really sent will open Instagram.

findings.where: from y=941 to y=2444 of the 1440x3120 frame, between the note that reads "and the bread - there is half a loaf in the tin" and the composer
findings.what: Four of the seven rows the capture's own report calls `whole_on_the_glass` render as nothing at all. Measured: a continuous 1503-pixel stretch (48.2 per cent of the frame height) in which no image row has more than 12 per cent of its width above grey level 150, and a Gaussian high-pass of the stretch shows only desk grain. Calibrating the thread against 02_chat.png (same region, same 480x1040 CSS viewport at dpr 3) gives origin y=321 px and 3 px per logical point - verified on 02_chat's three state lines at logical tops 587/618/649, predicted 2082/2175/2268 px, measured 2082/2174/2267 px. Rows 8074-8077 of 13_messenger_states sit at logical 249-697, i.e. px 1068-2412, entirely inside that empty stretch, and the thread's own bottom edge computes to 321 + 3*707.2 = 2443 px, exactly where the composer band begins at 2444. So the rows are inside the visible thread and paint nothing. Corroboration from the same report: `masks_composed: 4` for a frame it says holds seven torn sheets, and `paper_at_its_own_size: 240` against 1264 in 02_chat.png.
findings.why: The vanished rows are the ones this artifact exists to show: the reply row 0001MCJ1M05KVSSP7MN1H89FBP, two rows the report marks `sent`, and the refused row 0001MCJ1M05KVSSP7MN1H89FBF whose text the report gives as "it would not go" / "this phone is on an older version and cannot read that". `states_on_the_glass` claims {sent: 4, "it would not go": 1}; the picture carries one `sent` and no refusal. Row 01 is judged on delivery and read state being dependable, and the single frame that is supposed to prove the state vocabulary cannot be checked against its own claims - the refusal, the state a person most needs to trust, is not on the glass at all.

findings.where: row 8074 (the vanished stretch), and by absence every other chat capture in the set
findings.what: No delivered reply is visible anywhere in the evidence. `replies_on_the_glass` is {} in 02_chat.report.json, 06_unfolding.report.json, 08_state_propagating.report.json, 11_chat_scroll.report.json and 10_first_run.report.json; the set's only entry is 13's single reply at row 8074, which is inside the 1503-px empty stretch above. What is visible is the composer chip "answering yes - the tin one, by the door" in 13_messenger_states.png, which shows a reply being written, never one that landed and resolved to its target in the thread.
findings.why: Replies are a named capability in row 01. A capability that cannot be seen anywhere in the ten artifacts does not exist as far as this evidence goes, and a thread whose replies cannot be shown to render is one of the most common reasons a couple keeps a second messenger open.

findings.where: absent; DIFF.json labels it `absent`, MANIFEST.json and WHY_MISSING.json give the reason
findings.what: Every present artifact in the set was shot on one engine: MANIFEST.json records `browser: webkit` and all fifteen scene logs carry `"browser": "webkit"`. 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png are missing, with a standing reason - no /dev/kvm, adbd answered after 113 minutes and the framework never came up behind it. So no artifact shows the Android messenger doing anything.
findings.why: The reason is a measured machine fact, not an excuse, and I am not scoring the build down for the emulator. But row 01 is about a messenger the couple can rely on across both their phones, and half that claim has no evidence in the set at all. I can only say the PWA messenger holds up; whether the Android one does is unscored, and it cannot be scored full marks on evidence that does not exist.

findings.where: evidence/logs/11_chat_scroll.json `load`, and the same field in 01_pulse.json, 05_settings.json and 08_state_propagating.json
findings.what: A first launch against the year-deep history takes 8,551 ms to the first frame (`load.ms`, `store: fresh`), of which `made_of.the log` is 6,726 ms. The other three cold launches agree: 8,514 ms (6,513 the log), 8,427 ms (6,442) and 8,912 ms (6,838). Warm launches on the same profile are 2,181-2,708 ms with `made_of.everything` at 1,158-1,221 ms. No artifact in the set shows what is on the screen during those eight and a half seconds.
findings.why: Row 01 names "no spinner that outstays its welcome". Eight and a half seconds of nothing on the first open is well past welcome, and the set offers no frame of that interval to judge whether it is a spinner, a blank desk or a written waiting state - which is itself the finding, because the one interval most likely to break the row is the one interval nobody captured.

findings.where: the scrub strip below the video
findings.what: The readout reads "0:00 / 0:03" while logs/14_media_viewer.report.json gives `position_ms: 771` of `duration_ms: 2500` and the handle sits roughly 31 per cent along the bar. Elapsed is truncated to whole seconds, so it shows 0:00 for the first full second of any clip, and the 2.5-second file is labelled 0:03.
findings.why: A small thing, but it is the only media-viewer state the still can be checked against, and the number disagrees with the handle beside it. Row 01 asks for state a person can trust; a counter that reads zero while the playhead has visibly moved is a state that cannot be.

findings.what: ffprobe gives duration 5.376 s at 1080x2340, 125/2 fps, 336 frames. The brief's minimum for this artifact is 6 seconds, and MANIFEST.json records the shortfall itself: `minimum_seconds: 6`, `long_enough: false`.
findings.why: Not a row 01 capability, but the set's own manifest marks one of the ten artifacts as not meeting its stated minimum, and a report that opened the manifest and did not say so would be scoring on part of the evidence.

findings.where: frame 690, the four rows above and including the sent note
findings.what: Reading down: "tuesday soup / Thu 3 Sep - 19:55", "noor is heads down / Thu 3 Sep - 19:55", "noor is quiet / Thu 3 Sep - 19:58", then the person's own note "on my way - leaving in ten / Thu 3 Sep - 19:40 sent". The newest row on the glass carries a time eighteen minutes earlier than the rows above it. The report's `now` is 2026-09-03T19:40:00Z with `driven_ms: 13392`, so the near phone's clock reads 19:40:13 while every far-written row is stamped 19:54-19:58.
findings.why: I am filing this as minor rather than as an ordering fault, because WHY_MISSING.json says the far phone is `dart run tool/host_daemon.dart` - a separate process that is almost certainly on wall-clock time rather than on the app's driven clock, which makes this a fault in how the picture was taken. It is still worth naming: as shot, the clip shows a thread that reads 19:55, 19:58, 19:40 downwards, and a reader who did not have the scene file would read that as broken ordering after a reconnect.

findings.what: The scene shot to read the pocket back after the pushes returns `held_by_the_phone: []` with `and_it_is_empty_because: "the browser is holding nothing"`, and the report for that same crop reads `setup_showing: true`, `link: "connecting"`, `visible: []` - the phone being picked up is an unpaired fresh profile sitting on the setup checklist, which is what the crop shows.
findings.why: Nothing in the set shows a message reaching a phone that is not open. Push is not one of row 01's named capabilities, so this is minor for my row, but it means a message arriving while the app is closed is unproven in every direction the evidence runs.

what_is_working: The dense scroll is clean. Across all 300 frames of 11_chat_scroll.mp4 the fling log shows every frame moving exactly what the simulation asked - max |asked - moved| = 0.0, `frames_under_a_device_pixel: 0`, 8 throws, 27,645 logical px travelled of a 510,552 px thread. frames.json reports `repeated_frames: 0` and `longest_still_run: 0`. I measured the paper fraction of the thread area on every frame: it never falls below 0.291 and ink never below 0.382, so no frame goes blank or half-drawn.

The app's own cost during that scroll is modest. logs/scroll_webkit.json gives build_ms p50 7, p95 25; only 69 of 730 frames cost more than 16 ms to build and 19 more than 33 ms, with a single 569 ms outlier. Raster (p50 95 ms) is the software rasteriser on a machine with no GPU and the log says so, so I set it aside rather than charging it to the app.

I scanned for the emptied-row failure across the other clips and did not find it: 0 blank sheets of 166 sampled across 60 frames of 11_chat_scroll.mp4, 0 of 168 in 07_feeling_landing.mp4 and 0 of 159 in 15_authored_feeling.mp4. The seeded year renders reliably; the fault in 13 is confined to freshly composed rows.

The reconnect story is legible on the glass rather than only in a log. 08_state_propagating.mp4 shows the banner "can't reach the other phone. it'll go when it can.", the note held at "Thu 3 Sep - 19:40 / waiting to send", and the same note turning to "Thu 3 Sep - 19:40 sent" once the link is back. That is the right way to show it.

Delivery vocabulary is real and legible where it renders. 02_chat.png carries three "read" marks with a double tick, checked at 300 per cent in crops/02_chat_300_hand.png-scale detail and unambiguous; 13_messenger_states.png carries "edited" and "sent", two withdrawn notes reading "took this back", the partner-typing line "noor writing...", a reply chip in the composer and a live draft "the second one, then".

Search is genuinely broad. 12_search.png shows the query "morning" with 6 hits, the matched word highlighted in every result row, a type filter set to photographs alongside written/video/talking/feelings/state/dates/to do/rituals, person filters for noor and teo, and a range filter for this year.

Media holds up under volume. 04_moments.report.json reports 183 media items (115 photo, 54 voice note, 14 video) with `tiles_without_a_picture: 0`, `the_tiles_with_no_picture: []`, and 18 of 18 blobs asked for arrived. 14_media_viewer.png shows full-resolution video playing with a caption and a scrub bar.

The wire itself has been proven once, properly. coldstart.json records transport tailscale, two distinct node keys, two distinct 100.x addresses, and four event ids appearing in `spine_host_order` and `spine_client_order` in the same order. reliability.json's 22 capability rows all read ok with `duplicates: 0`, `events_host` = `events_client` = 177, `same_order_both_sides: true` and `ordering: monotonic` - on the local transport, which the file names honestly.
verdict: The messenger underneath this is more complete than most of what it would replace: text, photographs, video, voice notes, reactions, edits, withdrawals, typing, a live draft, sent/read/waiting/refused states, full-text and media search with person and range filters, and a media viewer are all present, and the year-deep scroll is clean - 300 frames that each moved exactly what was asked of them, with no blank or half-built row in 166 sheets I sampled. What stops the row at its floor is that the two places the evidence tests it hardest both fail. On the only reconnect anywhere in the set, the capture's own log records the one message that crossed it twice (`said_again`: times 2) and the thread growing by four rows for two events written, where all sixteen other arrivals in the set add exactly one; row 01 forbids duplicated messages in terms, and a headless harness reporting `duplicates: 0` on the local transport does not answer a duplicate that happened on the glass. That is the finding marked blocking and the one holding this row down. Alongside it, 13_messenger_states.png - the single frame whose job is to prove the state vocabulary - renders four of its seven claimed rows as nothing: 1503 pixels, 48.2 per cent of the frame, of bare desk where the reply, two sent rows and the refusal "this phone is on an older version and cannot read that" should be. Between them, the two failures mean the set contains no delivered reply at all and no refusal on the glass, so two of the row's named capabilities cannot be checked. Add an eight-and-a-half-second first launch nobody photographed, and a whole platform with no artifact to its name, and this is a messenger I would believe rather than one the evidence shows me. 19 of 30.
